I really wish that I could have programmed it using the buttons on the front of the dishwasher, though. I kept asking if it could be done, and never got an answer. Being able to just press start, or set the settings manually is all that I need. I must say that customer support for programming was outstanding, but I hope that I won't need to contact them again every time that I change phones.

Sentence (English): This was the only dishwasher available that met all my criteria (black door with a handle, stainless steel tub, and a disposal).
Comments (English): This was the only dishwasher available that met all my criteria (black door with a handle, stainless steel tub, and a disposal). I was concerned based on some other reviews, but so far I am happy with it.The 60 minute wash cycle is a nice option, but could use improvement. I keep my water heater at its lowest setting, and the water is not hot enough to clean the dishes in the dishwasher. (It loses heat as the cycle progresses, and starting with minimal heat to begin with isn't enough.) There is a heat boost option on the dishwasher, and with it the dishes come clean. Frustratingly, the heat boost option cannot be added to the 60 minute cycle. The shortest cycle that uses heat boost is the normal cycle; with the heat boost that cycle runs for 1:48. That is still less energy than keeping the water heater at a higher setting 24 hrs/day.I will echo some of the other reviews about the bottom rack. The way the tines are spaced, it's difficult to use all the space with smaller items, such as tall drinking glasses or glass food storage containers. It seems to be designed for dinner-sized plates and pots/pans. I use cast iron pans, so they stay out of the dishwasher. And I typically use salad-sized plates. In my previous dishwasher, that left room for other items on the bottom rack, but it's a challenge to get smaller items to balance and remain upright on the bottom rack. I have not investigated whether a replacement rack is available that better suits my preference.There is a dry function to add to a cycle, but I have always skipped the drying function on my old dishwasher to save energy. Opening the door shortly after the wash cycle is complete and the dishes are still hot allows the water to evaporate and air dry quickly. I appreciate this dishwasher's chime to indicate the cycle is complete so I know when to open the door to start the air-drying.

I was concerned based on some other reviews, but so far I am happy with it.The 60 minute wash cycle is a nice option, but could use improvement. I keep my water heater at its lowest setting, and the water is not hot enough to clean the dishes in the dishwasher. (It loses heat as the cycle progresses, and starting with minimal heat to begin with isn't enough.) There is a heat boost option on the dishwasher, and with it the dishes come clean. Frustratingly, the heat boost option cannot be added to the 60 minute cycle. The shortest cycle that uses heat boost is the normal cycle; with the heat boost that cycle runs for 1:48. That is still less energy than keeping the water heater at a higher setting 24 hrs/day.I will echo some of the other reviews about the bottom rack. The way the tines are spaced, it's difficult to use all the space with smaller items, such as tall drinking glasses or glass food storage containers. It seems to be designed for dinner-sized plates and pots/pans. I use cast iron pans, so they stay out of the dishwasher. And I typically use salad-sized plates. In my previous dishwasher, that left room for other items on the bottom rack, but it's a challenge to get smaller items to balance and remain upright on the bottom rack. I have not investigated whether a replacement rack is available that better suits my preference.There is a dry function to add to a cycle, but I have always skipped the drying function on my old dishwasher to save energy. Opening the door shortly after the wash cycle is complete and the dishes are still hot allows the water to evaporate and air dry quickly. I appreciate this dishwasher's chime to indicate the cycle is complete so I know when to open the door to start the air-drying.

Sentence (English): If you're like me, you look for quality and longevity with your appliance purchases.
Comments (English): [ This is the one your looking for ] || ---------------- || If you're like me, you look for quality and longevity with your appliance purchases. Buy once, cry once. I had a base model Bosch in my house when I bought it but an electrical surge took it out in the first month:( . I was looking to upgrade, and after weeks of research and video reviews, I narrowed it down to the KitchenAid 704 and the Bosch 800. My wife preferred the KitchenAid rack system, and I agreed it was superior. BUT for every 9 good reviews, it had there was that one reviewer who had an issue and got to experience the KitchenAid customer service and warranty process. This put doubt in my mind I couldn't shake compared to the minor complaints the Bosch had. This did put my marriage on the line, but let that speak to my confidence in this ultimate decision.I pulled the trigger on the new style Bosch 800 with the new adjustable spray function (there is an older version for about a hundred bucks less so pay attention to part numbers). All the connections were identical to the unit it was replacing so installation was a breeze. Comments (English): [ A WASTE OF MONEY, and TIME. ] || ---------------- || If you have half an hour of your time, to waste waiting for your oven to heat up to proper temperature this oven is for you. And, if you want to waste your time and money on ingredients for baking, this oven will never fail in that department. To start the baking feature: select "bake" on the oven knob, select your temperature, hit start, the buzzer will go off at the set temperature when that number is reached; but the analog temperature thermometer (which you need to buy on your own) placed inside the oven indicates at least 25 to 50 degrees under that indicated temperature. Even checking on a baking item in the oven by opening the door, the temperature will drop by 25 degrees. This electric oven is not efficient, properly calibrated, or safe to use. I have had a repair man adjust the oven temperature to an increase of 35 degrees. Even after that adjustment, I am still checking, waiting, wondering if the bake good is baked on the inside, which it is not. This electric oven in a complete waste of money. A poorly designed appliance.

Sentence (English): Hello, this is a genuine review purchased with my own money.
Comments (English): [ The dishwasher is truly my true love ] || ---------------- || Hello, this is a genuine review purchased with my own money. Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Set) Delivery Date: September 14, 2023 Reason for Purchase: Housekeeping for a family of three: my husband, myself, and our son. As we entered our seventh year of marriage, we began to experience some burnout with housekeeping, so I started looking into dishwashers to make our lives a little easier. Initially, I looked into 12-place set dishwashers because people around me said bigger is better. However, due to the layout of our home, we couldn't install a built-in unit in the lower kitchen cabinets, so I looked into 6-place set models. I chose this product after reading reviews of various brands and watching YouTube videos. Satisfaction: Genuine Review (Purchased with My Own Money): After receiving delivery on September 14th and using it for about three months, the result is that it is more than sufficient for a family of three. Based on our usual household routine, we combine the dishes from breakfast and lunch (which have small portions) and run it, and then run it once after dinner. So, we usually run it about twice. The 6-person capacity fits way more than I expected. It fits dishes, cutlery, and even large pots from a meal for three, so I'm freed from dishwashing except for the pre-wash. It is just sooooo good. The best part is that the biggest advantage is being able to organize and put away dishes without bending over. The compartments are well-designed, making it easy to separate plates, bowls, cups, and cutlery. I don't find cooking itself a hassle, but I used to get stressed about cleaning up and washing dishes. Because of that, whenever I felt tired or lazy, I would order takeout or eat out, but that has really decreased since I got the dishwasher. After enjoying a delicious meal with my family, I just rinse the dishes roughly with water and put them in—that's it! Pro tip: Since it was installed right next to the sink, the installer warned me to be careful not to let water get under the machine. So, I installed a splash guard next to it as well! No water gets in, and I'm using it perfectly fine! Overall Review: I can never go back to a life without a dishwasher. ----------------------------. January 10, 2025. This is a dishwasher I am still using with immense satisfaction. It fits a household of three perfectly. During my child's school holidays and on weekends, I run it once for breakfast, once for lunch, and once for dinner. On weekdays when my child goes to kindergarten, I run it once for dinner. I wash the large pots separately, and for the rest, I pre-wash them before putting them in the dishwasher. In our house, I don't stack dishes; I lay them down one by one. After enjoying a delicious meal with my family, I just rinse the dishes roughly with water and put them in—that's it! Pro tip: Since it was installed right next to the sink, the installer warned me to be careful not to let water get under the machine. So, I installed a splash guard next to it as well! This is a dishwasher I am still using with immense satisfaction. It fits a household of three perfectly. I wash the large pots separately, and for the rest, I pre-wash them before putting them in the dishwasher. In our house, I don't stack dishes; I lay them down one by one. It feels like the cleaning isn't as thorough when stacked, so I lay them down completely individually. Even so, it is suitable for a family of three's meal dishes. I am using it with great satisfaction, and I hope it stays with me for a long, long time without breaking down. Dishwashers are love. I hope my review is of at least a little help to you.

Sentence (English): This replaced an equivalent Kitchenaid (stainless steel interior and exterior) which worked very well for over 16 years.
Comments (English): This replaced an equivalent Kitchenaid (stainless steel interior and exterior) which worked very well for over 16 years. We replaced it because the plastic components inside were getting heat fatique and replacement parts would have been expensive. But the old Kuitchenaid was a reliable workhorse mechanically and owed us nothing. This new Kitchenaid is better than the previous one in being VERY quiet. It seems to clean gunked-up pots a bit better on the bottom rack , and the three-shelf arrangement allows more flexible and easier loading. There's definitely more interior space available. Items like serving utensils and kitchen knives clean well on the shallow top (3rd) rack. The Normal cycle seems to run a little long; we've experimented with the Express Wash and found it effective with normal dinner dishes. Dishes are dry at end of full cycle. Control buttons/lights are simple and straightforward. So far (about one month in including a lot of Thanksgiving cleanup) we're very satisfied. I installed the DW myself after HD's delivery, it was very straightforward into the existing standard DW space, hardwired, saving $250 and $50 disposal. If you have an outlet, you need to order a cord kit for this DW. HD had some delivery problems (drivers couldn't find our house due to their GPS malfunctioning) but the dispatcher and crew took an extra effort to get here so we didn't need to reschedule delivery. Bottom of carton was damp on delivery from water from factory testing - - delivery crew said this was normal, and the unit appeared totally new and unblemished, and I did find some residual water inside. Unpacking: the DW door was difficult to open out of box - - I thought I was possibly ignoring a shipping tab or a latch that needed removal - - but it was because the plastic PVC shipping liner between the door and gasket made it very tight - - just give it a good pull. Kitchenaid 800 customer service line actually reachable to confirm. Recommend watching the Kitchenaid installation video even if you're handy - - the tip to carefully score blue protective film on door before peeling it away made for a neater installation. Good performance and value so far, especially on sale at HD with free delivery and avoiding the installation charge.

Sentence (English): The built in water softener is a real plus.
Comments (English): [ Excellet Machine but.  ] || ---------------- || The built in water softener is a real plus. Dishes come out of this machine VERY clean and spot free. The racks for dishes are well designed, reasonably easy to use, and do a great job of space saving (so more dishes can be loaded) while providing adequate spacing for complete cleaning. But. The silverware basket is too small. I know you have that third drawer for silverware, but it's nearly useless to us. We have always simply pitched silverware into the basket without being very particular about its spacing or orientation, and it comes out clean. We don't need or want to use silverware racks that require careful orientation and placement of each piece of silverware. The machine needs a signal of some sort that a dishwashing cycle has been completed. This signal should remain on until manually cancelled by some means like opening the door. Projecting "COMPLETED" on the floor with the clever little light would be a good way to do this. This would be particularly useful in one or two person households where the machine isn't run every day.

It came with the new home we purchased and was brand new when we moved in.All I can say is I will never buy Whirlpool again after the experience I had with it. After the first year I was constantly fixing it. Either replacing the racks that were breaking or spray arms that would just stop spraying enough to clean anything. When it functioned as it should, it worked well but that was maybe 20% of its lifetime. But at that point, you're just replacing random parts hoping that was the issue. But then I seen the heating element was damaged and warped as well. It would have been over $600 in parts alone to repair.Overall I'd say I spent over half the cost of the dishwasher replacing parts over the 3 years we had it. If you google the model number and read the views on various websites you'll find anyone that wrote a review that had the dishwasher for a any amount of time, said it was constantly breaking down as well. Most reviews seem to be written after the first few uses. Which is why these companies are changing models after a couple of years.Perhaps all dishwashers are cut from the same cloth these days but I won't take my chances anymore with Whirlpool anyways. Replaced it with an LG with a 5 year warranty. And if I have issues with that I'll be purchasing a Bosch next.

Sentence (English): It's not a sexy as an induction cooktop or refrigerator with lcd screens but this is about as perfect as an appliance gets.
Comments (English): [ Never thought I'd be excited over a dishwasher ] || ---------------- || It's not a sexy as an induction cooktop or refrigerator with lcd screens but this is about as perfect as an appliance gets. It's lack of heating element was intriguing and made me question whether things would be dry, but after running the first load I was assured and amazed. We don't have many plastic items to wash but what we have never has a problem completely drying (we use rinse-aid as recommended). It's ridiculously quiet, so the red light that shines in the floor during the cycle is a great feature to know it's actually running. The “Air Dry” feature on the 500 series is great in our high desert climate. At the end of the cycle the door pops open about 8” and since the humidity level is so low where we live, it finishes drying by evaporation. The third rack for silverware and adjustable 2nd rack are now features I couldn't live without. The classic style silverware holder it comes with is too small to be useful and just takes up space that is better used for pots and pans. The only issues was getting it on the network to take advantage of the WiFi abilities but once I read it only works on 2.4Ghz networks I was able to sync it just fine. It's app is okay as far as appliances go, but you can set custom programs for different wash cycles, adjust the amount of rinse-aid it dispenses, set schedules for run times and start it when you are in bed and don't want to get cold when you forget to run it after supper. I like the soap pod counter in the app that you can track how many pods you have left. It cleans really well and the stainless steel interior looks flawless after each wash. The removable filter is easy to inspect and clean, although I haven't found anything in it after a month of daily use. We scape but don't rinse any dishes and so far it's been a dream… I actually can't wait to unload it every morning but maybe I'm just weird! This was worth the money and if Bosch's service record holds up, then I expect to have it for decades to come.

We don't have many plastic items to wash but what we have never has a problem completely drying (we use rinse-aid as recommended). It's ridiculously quiet, so the red light that shines in the floor during the cycle is a great feature to know it's actually running. The “Air Dry” feature on the 500 series is great in our high desert climate. At the end of the cycle the door pops open about 8” and since the humidity level is so low where we live, it finishes drying by evaporation. The third rack for silverware and adjustable 2nd rack are now features I couldn't live without. The classic style silverware holder it comes with is too small to be useful and just takes up space that is better used for pots and pans. The only issues was getting it on the network to take advantage of the WiFi abilities but once I read it only works on 2.4Ghz networks I was able to sync it just fine. It's app is okay as far as appliances go, but you can set custom programs for different wash cycles, adjust the amount of rinse-aid it dispenses, set schedules for run times and start it when you are in bed and don't want to get cold when you forget to run it after supper. I like the soap pod counter in the app that you can track how many pods you have left. It cleans really well and the stainless steel interior looks flawless after each wash. The removable filter is easy to inspect and clean, although I haven't found anything in it after a month of daily use. We scape but don't rinse any dishes and so far it's been a dream… I actually can't wait to unload it every morning but maybe I'm just weird! This was worth the money and if Bosch's service record holds up, then I expect to have it for decades to come.

Sentence (English): Despite being $900 item, and despite being the same external size as all standard dishwashers, the interior is somehow tiny.
Comments (English): [ Size, controls, drying=poor; Lowe's service=worse ] || ---------------- || Despite being $900 item, and despite being the same external size as all standard dishwashers, the interior is somehow tiny. So instead of leisurely plunking dishes in the washer over the course of a few days it pretty much fills up with one sink-full of dishes and then you have to run it. Also "running it" has the typical issues of many newer DW's apparently--you can't tell if you've turned it on or off, it's unclear how to select cycles (pushing the buttons which appear to be dedicated to only selecting "normal", "heavy", etc. seems to do nothing. but then sometimes does! But then when you close/start the unit it doesn't), if you open the unit before cycle ends you will never get it to start again and finish the cycle. It doesn't dry all the way; there's always tepid water in the bay that already stinks a little. ALSO it was delivered wet. Was this a display model? What is water doing in the bottom of the bay? Why is it leaking out the door during install? Also why is a brand-new unit leaking at all? There should be no broken seals or grommets anywhere in a $900 brand new appliance. The silverware caddies do not "lock" into place--they have little tabs that appear to be meant to hook over the large rack when they set in place, but instead the little tabs don't make contact with anything. They almost appear to be made for a different model? Consequently, the entire caddy/rack (there are 2) flop all over the place, and easily spill just by rolling out the dishrack--adding to the overall poor experience of a cramped interior, with puddles of not-sterile water, with silverware messily dumped. My previous three apartments had what looked like 10-15 year old DW's that despite being the same external size were larger inside, turned on/off/paused/changed cycle easily by simply pushing the buttons as they were labeled and without reading any instructions, AND got everything clean and dried. And the silverware caddies just fit in place--I don't even know how this could be designed otherwise. Dishwashers are not new technology. They were figured out a long time ago. So how is this brand-new item that's definitely more expensive than those others so much worse? I called Lowe's and they said the return policy was 48 HOURS! This thing has been installed for a week, and I'd be willing to do exchange-only and simply go for a more expensive item. The customer service personnel sumbled through a sentence and simply hung up. I won't buy a single thumbtack from Lowe's ever again, and I won't go near this brand. Not sure what the thinking is, but yeah I wouldn't recommend this item, and I wouldn't recommend Lowe's since they have such a scummy policy especially when peddling junk.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher looks like it is the same size as all of my other diswhashers.
Comments (English): [ Very Disappointed ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher looks like it is the same size as all of my other diswhashers. However, it holds about 25% fewer items than any of the others. Whoever designed the interior layout has obviously never loaded a dishwasher with things that people normally use. The foward facing racks on the lower shelf are so close together that it is not possible to put normal size dinner dishes side by side. Maybe we should learn to use only dessert size dishes? The larger right facing racks in the rear of the lower shelf must be lowered flat if you want to wash a salad bowl, a cassarole dish or several smaller mixing bowls. The middle shelf accepts coffee mugs in the area originally designed for stemware (with the stemware holder folded up), unless you want to hang your mugs on top of a prong. Cereal dishes have to be hung over a prong or two. A normal size soup ladle has no logical place at all. Small glasses do have a place, thankfully. The very narrow top shelf is good for eating utensils, but is too small for cooking utensils, such as a spatula. Perhaps Bosch thinks everyone wants to run their dishwasher from an Ap, but I dont. I would much prefer a well-designed and more flexible interior. The machine washes well, but since I have to run it much more often than my other machines due to its space/design limitations, I am very frustrated. BTW, we are a two person family. I would definitely not recommend this machine for a larger family.

Sentence (English): We owned a Bosch dishwasher for 12 years and loved it.
Comments (English): [ Bosch's game has gone downhill ] || ---------------- || We owned a Bosch dishwasher for 12 years and loved it. This one. not so much. First off it does not dry the dishes. We have changed all the settings to maximize the drying-no luck. The third rack is always wet and drips down on the other 2 racks. The dishwasher is panelized but the springs that came with the unit were so strong that the door would snap your fingers off. Bosch authorized a service tech to change the door springs (thank you). There are a lot of other nits about this dishwasher that are annoying. For instance, when the dishwasher is clean and you open the door the "clean" light only stays on for around 3 seconds and then disappears. The manual says it beeps when done but we have had 2 of these (the first one's motor died after 5 days and was replaced) and neither one beeped at cycle end. The racks are not as well organized as our old one. It is quiet and I'm sure energy efficient but when you consider the poor drying, the racks that are not well organized and the other annoying features, we are disappointed. We wish we had our 12 year old Bosch back.

Sentence (English): We just replaced our 25 year old Kitchen Aid dishwasher with a Bosch 800 series dishwasher after reading reviews.
Comments (English): [ Excellent cleaning, very quite, some fcns need app ] || ---------------- || We just replaced our 25 year old Kitchen Aid dishwasher with a Bosch 800 series dishwasher after reading reviews. I was skeptical about all the good reviews regarding quietness, cleaning ability, and especially drying ability with Zeolite rather than a drying coil. After using for a month, I understand that the reviews were accurate. Only two minor complaints: 1) you need to use the app to enter machine clean or eco mode, or to customize lower cleaning quadrants. No dishwasher should require an app to access features. 2) The glasses rack is also a little odd in terms of our glass sizes. Either a bit too large, or a bit to small, and the features designed to hold glasses at a slant simply doesn't work with at least half of our glasses/cups, leaving water on the top of some glasses and cups even after Zeolite drying. These are minor complaints though. As I started out in this review, it is a fantastic dishwasher for excellent clean / quite, and good drying capabilities. I'd definitely purchase it again.

Sentence (English): I've never liked dishwashers.
Comments (English): [ Never going back to hand washing dishes! ] || ---------------- || I've never liked dishwashers. Growing up, they never got the dishes clean and always left residue on the dishes so I decided to forever hand wash dishes. My fiance decided he wanted a dishwasher (since I don't have time to hand wash dishes every day). We had some specifications like a stainless steel tub, autosensing, etc. This dishwasher is EVERYTHING we wanted and more! Totally changed my mind about dishwashers. We've had this dishwasher for nearly two months now and I would absolutely never go back to hand washing all of our dishes. We use the Cascade Platinum Plus dishwashing packs, and the Cascade rinseaid (same as the samples that come with it). Once a moth we pop in a Cascade dishashing cleaner pod and empty out any gunk from the filter in the bottom (easy to reach, open, and clean! ). We make sure to scrape and rinse off any leftover food we can, load it in the dishwasher, and everything comes out perfectly clean every single time! Glass, ceramic, and metal items come out the best, though there are water droplet marks leftover on plastic Tupperware. It's not dirty though, I just take a towel, rub it over the plastic, and the droplets disappear! There are more features we like including the bacteria resistant surfaces for high touch areas, it's 10000% easy to clean, there are bottle jets for bottles up top as well as jets beneath the silverware holder (ALL of our silverware is pristine every time) and we can adjust the height of the racks (as well as take out the third rack up top if we need more room). We haven't tried the app or the wifi features yet since we just run it on autosensing and let it do its thing! I highly recommend this dishwasher, especially if you are a skeptic like I was!

In the process they chipped 2 steps while bringing the old unit out of the house since they did not use straps to carry out, were not strong enough, and dropped on stairs! After an hour, since the person did not understand what a portable dishwasher was, I drove to the Ridgedale store again. I was told by the appliance department man, who had worked at Sears in their appliance department, that the charge was $25 to remove from the box and to add wheels. I told him that was new information to me and would have paid that small amount, but I was not told that. After he kept telling me the same $25 fee, I asked him to try to ring it up to see where the 1st salesperson went wrong. After repeated requests, because I wanted to solve the problem, he attempted to enter a purchase and he said there was not a screen to order haul away either, so he was incorrect and not sure what to say now. Gave me the phone number to the headquarters off 494 and Penn, to the Large Appliance Resolution Team and when I called, I ended up offshore again, in the Philippines. Called again the following day and no one knew what the Large Appliance Resolution Team was so I requested they pick up the dishwasher, I was done. If I had the ability to remove from the box, set on its side to attached wheels and set upright again, I would have done it, but I do not.Always have relied on Best Buy for value, customer service and great products. But the false promises, confusion of staff, Oscar at Pulse Logistics dropping the old dishwasher on the new concrete steps is significant to possibly change where I spend my money. Reported broken steps 11-30-23 and have not heard back yet on that claim. I do not expect perfection, just for people and companies to do what they promise. Sentence (English): We had a Maytag dishwasher in a previous home that we were very happy with.
Comments (English): [ Delivered Damaged and No Quick Rinse Option ] || ---------------- || We had a Maytag dishwasher in a previous home that we were very happy with. Unfortunately, so far this experience with Maytag and Lowe's has not gone well. The dishwasher arrived with a dent in the rear top corner. Since it is very hard to spot from the inside we decided to live with it rather than go through the hassle of returning it and trying to get another one delivered. After installing it I found there is a discoloration on the control panel (looks like something splashed on it and discolored that area) and the lower basket had a broken roller. It took me over an hour online with Maytag to get them to send out a new roller. Lowe's also delivered the wrong waterline hookup. It was cheaper than the one I ordered and paid for. So another 2 hours to go to the store and deal with getting it returned and getting the right one. Later, after installing it, I discovered that there is no quick rinse option. I've never had a dishwasher without this feature. What is Maytag thinking! After reading more reviews I can see I'm not the only one frustrated by this. The good news is that it seems to clean the dishes quite well, but overall I'm disappointed with both Maytag and Lowes.

And in order to change to a 14-player version, I searched various places such as YouTube, Naver, Ku*, SK public website, etc. for a while to study function reviews, prices, etc., and then I found a live broadcast preview on the public website and waited. I purchased it on Wednesday, the day of the live broadcast, and also won the 1st pitch induction.^^. For installation, we had three visits sequentially, including a preliminary visit on Thursday, reform work on Saturday morning, and dishwasher installation that afternoon. First of all, Baek**, the construction manager sent by Seven*** who was in charge of the construction, was really kind. Usually, when dishwasher construction is done in an apartment, there are posts asking for the community's understanding that the noise is louder than expected. In our house, the construction manager took it out to the stairs outside the front door (even though we didn't ask for it) and cut it, etc. I only closed the middle door of my house and left the front door wide open, but there wasn't much noise. They carried out the work kindly from start to finish, and even took into account the differences in height between the left and right sides during construction. Installation master Hong**, who visited around 12 noon, also calmly and meticulously installed the product. They called us from time to time to explain things, and even removed and collected the previously used SK 6-seater. On Saturday evening, the day of installation, I filled the 14-person container with frying pans and pots and turned it around. Since I usually give trays to children, even though the bowl size is large, I was able to easily feed four trays together. Sentence (English): This is our 2nd BOSCH.
Comments (English): [ Almost perfect ] || ---------------- || This is our 2nd BOSCH. The first was a replacement in our previous home and we had a great experience and were confident in purchasing another. In all honesty, I was hunting for an old fashioned push button front model. I think the 100 Series would have been just fine and would get the job done. Unfortunately, I could not get a hold of one as it was made a few seasons ago. So, after much research along the BOSCH offerings I arrived at the 300 model as it provided a good balance of features for as reasonable a price I could find. While we have only had the washer for about a month, it was installed prior to Thanksgiving and has been run almost daily since. To no surprise, it's quiet and does the job of cleaning the dishes very well. Know 2 things, the cycle can run up to 3 hours so what you're saving in water you may use in electricity so run it during off-peak hours and the second is the utensil rack takes a little getting used to as you can't just throw things into the dishwasher (I enjoy loading it properly), but man it does a great job! The only ask I have for Bosch is that the clean light remains illuminated after the cycle is complete at least until the door is opened.

Sentence (English): We have been using this dishwasher for 5.5 months and I absolutely love it.
Comments (English): [ Very happy after 5.5 months of use ] || ---------------- || We have been using this dishwasher for 5.5 months and I absolutely love it. I have waited to do a review to give a more helpful assessment. (Mine has last 3 digits of model number as KBS, not KPS, and I don't think mine has the PrintShield feature - but fingerprints are not a problem.) I LOVE the third rack! Almost all my utensils and odd items fit there. It seems like this dishwasher holds twice as much as my old one did, due to that 3rd rack. I love the ProWash & ProDry settings and use them almost every time. The fan is very useful for drying dishes better than with just high heat, and it's not so hard on my plastic containers. Every dish is not completely dry, but it's way better than before.I can't believe how clean the dishes come out. I will admit that we use Cascade Platinum pods - a rare top-brand item we buy (on sale! ) because it works so well - but I used them with the old dishwasher also and this one is just amazing. I put dishes in usually without rinsing AT ALL, even with baked on food like a lasagna dish - and they almost always come totally clean! Even my plastic containers don't come out greasy! It is a dream come true haha! It is also nice and quiet. We forget it's on. Yes, as in other reviews, I have had to learn how to best load this one and change some habits. But to have the sink free of dirty dishes when everyone loads directly into the dishwasher is well worth changing some things. If I had to say something negative - I don't love the controls on the very top edge of the door. I still accidentally turn it on when loading sometimes, and press cancel to stop it. I'd rather have the controls on the front and not the very top (not visible until you open the door), but the whole thing works so well that the placement of controls is not a deal at all to me.

Every dish is not completely dry, but it's way better than before.I can't believe how clean the dishes come out. I will admit that we use Cascade Platinum pods - a rare top-brand item we buy (on sale!) because it works so well - but I used them with the old dishwasher also and this one is just amazing.  I put dishes in usually without rinsing AT ALL, even with baked on food like a lasagna dish - and they almost always come totally clean!! Even my plastic containers don't come out greasy! It is a dream come true haha! It is also nice and quiet.  We forget it's on. Yes, as in other reviews, I have had to learn how to best load this one and change some habits.  But to have the sink free of dirty dishes when everyone loads directly into the dishwasher is well worth changing some things. If I had to say something negative - I don't love the controls on the very top edge of the door.  I still accidentally turn it on when loading sometimes, and press cancel to stop it.  I'd rather have the controls on the front and not the very top (not visible until you open the door), but the whole thing works so well that the placement of controls is not a deal at all to me.

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher to replace a 20 year old one that had started to leak and I'm sorry I did rather than just fixing the old one.
Comments (English): [ Greatly disappointed ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher to replace a 20 year old one that had started to leak and I'm sorry I did rather than just fixing the old one. This one doesn't have several features that are advertised on the Whirlpool website such as a fold down cup shelf, sliding bowl tines in the lower rack or a stemware holder. The lower rack is configured poorly and doesn't fit many of my dishes. I can only get about 70% as many dishes into it as I could with my previous dishwasher. Luckily, I kept the lower rack from the old dishwasher and it fits in the new one. The old rack allows all the tines to fold down, it has two silverware bins that are much easier to work with (the diagonal slots in the Whirlpool silverware bins are awkward to use since they force you to orient the silverware in directions that cause the spoons and forks to interfere with each other. The one gripe I had with the old dishwasher was that the small holes in the spinners got plugged up with debris quite regularly and there was no way to open up the spinners to clean them out. I had hoped that the Whirlpool dishwasher would have spinners that would be easier to clean, but it appears that the spinners on this new one are just like the ones on my old dishwasher. We will see if they get clogged as easily as my old one and if it's easy (or even possible) to clean them.I really wish I had kept the upper rack from the old dishwasher as it also was much better configured than the new one. It had fold down stemware holders, fold down tines on the side channels which were very good at supporting glasses, and dish slots that were just right for small cat food bowls. Disappointlngly, the new Whirlpool dishwasher has none of these features.

Sentence (English): If I could give Bosch and Lowe's, zero stars on this review I would.
Comments (English): [ DO NOT BUY or at least KNOW what you're getting ] || ---------------- || If I could give Bosch and Lowe's, zero stars on this review I would.First, the Bosch dishwasher is horrible. It leaves dishes soaking wet. The second time we ran the dishwasher we ran it at night and let the dishes sit overnight. It had been 12 hours since the cycle had completed including the “heated drying cycle” and using Jet Dry (as suggested). When we opened the dishwasher, the inside of the washer was completely wet. Ceramic dishes were somewhat dry, but everything else - including the entire inside of the dishwasher and all its trays - was dripping wet. It doesn't take a genius to understand that in no time at all, this dishwasher will stink due to moisture. After doing some research we learned that this is not a malfunction of the dishwasher but is actually by design. There's no heating element. So, unless you're fine with hand-drying your dishes before they are put away, don't buy a Bosch. For me, it feels more efficient to just hand wash and dry my dishes. Second, Lowes. Our dishwasher was delivered on a Thursday, installed on Monday and we went to Lowes to express our displeasure on Saturday. They would do nothing. Lowes's policy is that unless your purchase is on the Lowes credit card, you only have 48 hours to make a return. (You get 30 days if you use their credit card.) 48 hours is a meaningless amount of time to return an appliance that needs professional installation. This policy proves that Lowes values profit over people. It isn't as if they don't take appliance returns. They just want to force customers to use their credit card. We purchased a $3600 double oven from Lowes earlier this year. (They never mentioned this policy BTW.) We are currently in the market for a (different) dishwasher and a microwave. Next year, we'll likely replace our refrigerator. We will NEVER buy another appliance from Lowes. At this point, I'm not sure when I'll even shop there. I'm so disappointed in both of these brands.

A ver si este dura lo mismo.

Sentence (English): The best thing about this model is that it's a few centimeters larger than the "regular" model, which provides more interior space.
Comments (English): [ Size matters. ] || ---------------- || The best thing about this model is that it's a few centimeters larger than the "regular" model, which provides more interior space. This is especially useful when the dishwasher is fully loaded and has large pots and pans. Plus, since it fits right into the recess, I avoid having to use the dishwasher legs, which would eventually buckle and have to be readjusted. What I liked least is the cutlery tray. The previous one had a basket, and I didn't have to position the cutlery, just dump it into the basket. The build quality seems worse than the 20-year-old model it replaces. Let's see if this one lasts as long.
Comments (Original): [ El tamaño importa. ] || ---------------- || Lo mejor de este modelo es que es unos centímetros más grande que los 'normales', con lo que se consigue un espacio interior mayor. El anterior era de cesta y no tenía que colocar los cubiertos en posición, sólo echarlos en la cesta. La calidad de construcción parece peor que el que sustituye que tiene 20 años. A ver si este dura lo mismo.

Sentence (English): I can never go back to the days when I didn't have one!
Comments (English): I can never go back to the days when I didn't have one! I heard so many people around me say that a dishwasher is a must-have. After having a baby and starting solid foods, the amount of dishes to wash—bottles, baby dishes, etc.—was overwhelming, so I decided to buy a dishwasher to lighten the workload. After searching around, I found two popular products, but I chose the Samsung one! I’ll explain why now. 1. Cleaning Power. Isn't this the basic standard of a dishwasher? It's pointless to even mention it, so I'll skip that part! 2. Capacity. It is a 6-place setting, so while it is smaller compared to larger sizes, I wanted a size that could comfortably fit frying pans and pots. However, among the two famous products, the other brand seemed too small. My kitchen isn't particularly spacious, so I was a bit worried about the size, but after measuring it, it seemed okay, so I bought it. And guess what? It fits perfectly! I am extremely satisfied. 3. Design. Since a dishwasher is an appliance, design is also something you can't ignore. For me, if the design isn't good, it bothers me every time I use it. The white color was so pretty, and I am very satisfied with the design, which is simple and classic. Since it is touch-operated rather than having separate buttons, it is clean and sleek without any unnecessary clutter. After using it for a few months, I can say it looks beautiful even after a long time. Now that I have used it, I don't think I could ever go back to not having it. Never. It is so, so good. Raising a baby is busy enough, but it is great to not have to get stressed looking at the piles of dishes. Being able to take better care of the baby while the dishwasher is running is also a plus. I hope this helps those of you in a similar situation! ^^

After having a baby and starting solid foods, the amount of dishes to wash—bottles, baby dishes, etc.—was overwhelming, so I decided to buy a dishwasher to lighten the workload. After searching around, I found two popular products, but I chose the Samsung one! I’ll explain why now. 1. Cleaning Power. Isn't this the basic standard of a dishwasher? It's pointless to even mention it, so I'll skip that part! 2. Capacity. It is a 6-place setting, so while it is smaller compared to larger sizes, I wanted a size that could comfortably fit frying pans and pots. However, among the two famous products, the other brand seemed too small. My kitchen isn't particularly spacious, so I was a bit worried about the size, but after measuring it, it seemed okay, so I bought it. And guess what? It fits perfectly! I am extremely satisfied. 3. Design. Since a dishwasher is an appliance, design is also something you can't ignore. For me, if the design isn't good, it bothers me every time I use it. The white color was so pretty, and I am very satisfied with the design, which is simple and classic. Since it is touch-operated rather than having separate buttons, it is clean and sleek without any unnecessary clutter. After using it for a few months, I can say it looks beautiful even after a long time. Now that I have used it, I don't think I could ever go back to not having it. Never. It is so, so good. Raising a baby is busy enough, but it is great to not have to get stressed looking at the piles of dishes. Being able to take better care of the baby while the dishwasher is running is also a plus. I hope this helps those of you in a similar situation! ^^

Comments (English): [ It's OK, but With Some Flaws. ] || ---------------- || This unit is whisper quiet as advertised - VERY quiet. Also, it seems to do a very good job cleaning the dishes. The problems I have with it are as follows: 1) When the lower front kickplate was installed it seems to pull on the rubber grommet hanging down from the bottom of the dishwasher which gets tucked behind the kickplate. Because of this, tension gets put on the door and prevents the door from opening completely flat. The workaround was to put the rubber grommet in FRONT of the kickplate, but it does not look a clean down there. Without this workaround, it would have to go. 2) Still, there is too much friction on the door which prevents it from opening easily and effortlessly. To get the door to lie flat, one must bend over EVERY TIME and press the door down all the way. Not good, Samsung. 3) Aside from the friction on the door, the opening and closing resistance is NOT uniform - part of the way it moves easier and part of the way it requires MORE effort to open and close. Also NOT GOOD. Lastly. 4) Other dishwashers we've had allow you to keep the door slightly ajar. Not this one - the door is either open or closed. No middle ground here. It always has to be locked shut or it sticks out too far otherwise. Other models allow the door to remain slightly open without having to lock it shut.Knowing these items now, I probably would not re-purchase this dishwasher in spite of it's quietness and dish cleaning capabilities. It's the usability issues that I'm not to fond of, and that counts for quite a bit. 3 Stars at best here.(We purchased it because it seemed to have decent ratings and Samsung offered free installation and removal of the old unit), which was a nice offer.That's it!

Sentence (English): Excellent dishwasher for areas that have hard water.
Comments (English): [ Dishwasher that works ] || ---------------- || Excellent dishwasher for areas that have hard water. After months of dirty dishes froam a brand that starts with an S, this dishwasheer works flawlessly. The water softening feature that requires special dishwasher salt, is essential for the hard water that is prevelent in Orange County California. This dishwasher has lots of options for loading bowls, plates, silverware, & pots. The third cutlery shelve is a little difficult to load; however, every piece gets clean & you can grab the cutlery by its handle. This tray is also great for ladles, spatulas, & tongs. We can hardly hear this dishwasher. Even plastic ware comes out almost completely dry. I also appreciate the manual filter that can be easily removed & rinsed after each wash cycle. I had to remove about eight screws in order to remove & clean the closed filter in our previous dishwasher. I will never buy another dishwasher that doesn't have an easy to clean filter.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher is definitely roomy, and was able to accommodate about 3 days worth of dishwasher safe dishes/large items like stainless steel pans.
Comments (English): [ Roomy, and clean after one wash! ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher is definitely roomy, and was able to accommodate about 3 days worth of dishwasher safe dishes/large items like stainless steel pans. My dishes come out clean without needing to prewash. The load times are long, but it does the job in that time for sure. A lot of people complain about the dishwasher not drying the dishes, but with the boost setting, with the residual heat, a lot of my dishes are dry from the bottom rack. The main dishes that don't dry are the ones that can't hold heat, like dishwasher safe tupperware, or the tops of cups/mugs. With the door open, the dishes dry within a few hours. My one major gripe with this is the water left at the bottom. I'm not a huge fan of the water being left in it, as we don't use enough dishes during one day to run the dishwasher constantly. Maybe 2 days worth of dishes at the earliest. Just worried about any micro-organisms is all, but the dishwasher does get pretty hot to potentially kill some organisms. There is also a sanitization option.

I'm a weekend couple, so I live with my child almost exclusively, and even though I only cook for him in the evening at home, the dishwashing container is still full. When I come home from work, cook, feed, and clean up, I keep putting off doing it tomorrow or later when I see the dishwashing container full. Since I worked through the existing water purifier hole, I didn't drill a separate hole. *****Cleaning power: ****** What can I say about the cleaning power? It's so hot and squeaky. I think it must have eaten a lot of bacteria. The frying pan, pot, glass cup, spoon, and chopsticks were all cleaned well. It works, and the door opens automatically, so I don't have to open it separately when I go out or sleep, which is nice. Don't worry and buy it! Your quality of life will improve. If you worry, you'll just end up doing the dishes more often. The kitchen is now tidier^^

Sentence (English): My husband, me, and our one-year-old baby live together.
Comments (English): [ 3 person household ] || ---------------- || My husband, me, and our one-year-old baby live together. I bought this because I was getting increasingly stressed and doing the dishes was such a hassle after I got pregnant. I was hesitant because I heard there are a lot of fakes on Coupang, but I bought it because the installation was fast, and I was really happy that it was actually quick. The technician was kind and was working even though it was Saturday. I ordered around 11 PM on Thursday and had it installed on Saturday afternoon. I tried using it for the first time, but maybe because it was my first time, I didn't know how to stack the dishes. It also felt a bit small. I think I'll eventually have to wash things like woks and pots by hand. I ran it and went out for three hours, and when I came back, some dishes weren't completely dry. I managed to wash them roughly, but I was baffled that some items weren't cleaned properly even though I pre-washed them and wiped off grease with a paper towel before running it. Still, it's nice that if I run it before bed, there are no dishes to wash when I wake up. I didn't drill a hole and just ran the cord through the detergent dispenser opening. Since I live in an older apartment building, I didn't have enough space, so I placed it next to the gas stove. I don't think I can use one of the large burners. I recommend it for a two-person household. I bought it on Samgugu, but it's even cheaper now. The prices fluctuate so much that you really need to check carefully before buying. Also, I didn't know this, but a new model with hot air drying has been released. It costs twice as much, but if I had known, I probably would have bought that one even at the price. The structure is slightly different, so it fits more dishes, and it has a separate baby bottle sterilization mode. Also, the current one doesn't dry very well, but the new model seems capable of complete drying. Please check the official website for details.

Sentence (English): This unit is whisper quiet as advertised - VERY quiet.
Comments (English): [ It's OK, but With Some Flaws. ] || ---------------- || This unit is whisper quiet as advertised - VERY quiet. Also, it seems to do a very good job cleaning the dishes. The problems I have with it are as follows: . 1) When the lower front kickplate was installed it seems to pull on the rubber grommet hanging down from the bottom of the dishwasher which gets tucked behind the kickplate. Because of this, tension gets put on the door and prevents the door from opening completely flat. The workaround was to put the rubber grommet in FRONT of the kickplate, but it does not look a clean down there. Without this workaround, it would have to go. 2) Still, there is too much friction on the door which prevents it from opening easily and effortlessly. To get the door to lie flat, one must bend over EVERY TIME and press the door down all the way. Not good, Samsung. 3) Aside from the friction on the door, the opening and closing resistance is NOT uniform - part of the way it moves easier and part of the way it requires MORE effort to open and close. Also NOT GOOD. Lastly. 4) Other dishwashers we've had allow you to keep the door slightly ajar. Not this one - the door is either open or closed. No middle ground here. It always has to be locked shut or it sticks out too far otherwise. Other models allow the door to remain slightly open without having to lock it shut. Knowing these items now, I probably would not re-purchase this dishwasher in spite of it's quietness and dish cleaning capabilities. It's the usability issues that I'm not to fond of, and that counts for quite a bit. 3 Stars at best here. (We purchased it because it seemed to have decent ratings and Samsung offered free installation and removal of the old unit), which was a nice offer. That's it!

Sentence (English): While aesthetically I would give this 5 stars, practically I give it a 3.5.
Comments (English): [ It's pretty but.  ] || ---------------- || While aesthetically I would give this 5 stars, practically I give it a 3.5. We bought this mainly for looks when replacing all of our kitchen appliances and loved the sleek black look. According to the size it was the same as what it was replacing so we assumed we were mostly just getting an upgrade as far as efficiency and looks. It just FEELS so much smaller. I don't know why but it feels like everything just barely fits. We couldnt even use the very slim top tray because then our glassware wouldnt fit on the top, and we had to drop the \"top\" so now tall cooking utensils dont fit in the holder on the bottom - we still have to store them flat on the \"top\" but that is taking space away from the top-shelf wash only items. The only great thing about the functionality of this dishwasher is that it pops open after the cycle to allow air in to actually dry the dishes (instead of puddles on mug bottoms, etc.). If you are replacing for looks - I would highly recommend this! However, after using it a bit I would not recommend it for functionality. There are better dishwashers on the market that just dont look as sleek!
